To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there is an effective immune response in the peripheral whole blood of patients in remission from cancer and flu-like symptoms, and 2) the specific fluorescent GP1R binding patterns in the cytoplamic area of nucleated cells, in the nuclear area of segmented neutrophil and in the cytoplasic areas of small lymphocytic-like elements may be associated with a favorable prognosis in cancer patients.

1) the presence of fluorescent GP1R targets in peripheral blood samples of patients in remission may be associated with a favorable prognosis, 2) the presence of GP1R-binding in the peripheral blood of patients who have recovered from flu-like symptoms suggests a favorable prognosis, and 3) the presence of specific binding patterns in the peripheral whole blood smers of patients in remisson may be associated with favorable prognosis and its use as a liquid biopsy.

we found a specific pattern of binding targets of a fluorescent granzyme B-like synthetic peptide (GP1R) in peripheral blood samples of patients with cancer or flu-like symptoms in remission and a negative control, and the specific binding pattern in patients in remission is associated with an effective immunological response to the disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential use of GP1R-binding pattern in peripheral blood smears as a liquid biopsy in patients with cancer and viral infection.
the detection of a fluorescent synthetic GrzB-like peptide in peripheral blood of cancer and flu-infected patients.
the potential association between specific fluorescent Granzyme B peptide binding patterns and effective immune response, prognosis and survival in patients with cancer and viral infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GP1R binding patterns in peripheral blood may be associated with the immune status of patients with cancer or viral infection, and may have clinical significance.
the GP1R binding targets are detectable in the peripheral blood of patients in remission with cancer and flu-like symptoms.

1) GP1R targets are detectable in the peripheral blood of cancer patients, 2) GP1R-targets may be associated with a favorable prognosis, 3) GP1R is not a specific marker for cancer, 4) the GP1R-target binding pattern in peripheral blood smears may be associated with specific immune response, and 5) a specific GP1R-target pattern may be associated and used as a liquid biopsy to monitor an effective immune response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the GP1R binding targets in the peripheral blood of patients in remission are: 1. mostly in the cytosolic areas of nucleated cell elements in patients with cancer who have a better prognosis, 2. mostly in the nuclear area of segmented neutrophil-like cells in patients with viral infections, and 3. in the cytosol of small lymphocyte elements and in large cell elements in a patient with advanced pancreatic carcinoma who has a poor prognosis.
the GP1R peptide may be a potential marker for an effective immune response and a favorable prognosis in cancer and viral infection.

GP1R-binding pattern in peripheral whole blood smear of patients in remission may indicate a favorable prognosis, and that GP1R may serve as a potential liquid biopsy marker for an effective immune response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
specific binding patterns for GP1R in peripheral whole blood samples are potentially useful for monitoring immune response to tumor and viral infection progression.

specific fluorescent patterns in peripheral blood smears may be used as a liquid biopsy to indicate the presence of an effective immune response and a favorable prognosis in patients with cancer and viral infection.
